title: Why Do Dogs Love Climbing Into Boxes?
description:
Cats aren't the only ones. Here's why an empty box is suddenly the most interesting thing in the house.

script: A brand new cardboard box shows up in the living room, and somehow it becomes more interesting than every toy your dog already owns. Part of that is pure novelty, dogs are drawn to new smells, new textures, and new shapes in their environment, and a box checks every one of those boxes, literally. There's also a den instinct at play, a lot of dogs are descended from denning animals, and a small enclosed space with walls on multiple sides can feel instinctively safe and cozy, similar to why some dogs love crawling under furniture or blankets. Boxes also carry a ton of interesting scent information, especially if they shipped from somewhere or held groceries, so sniffing one out is genuinely enriching for a dog's nose. And for some dogs it's simply about the texture, cardboard is satisfying to chew, scratch, and dig at, which taps into completely normal exploratory behavior. So if your dog is more excited about the empty box than what came inside it, that's not weird at all, that's just a dog following several very natural instincts at once.
